subtitle: All the news that's fit to Fingerprint

lead.headline: Comcast to Spin Off NBCUniversal and Sky Into Standalone Company
lead.dek: Tax-free split hands the streamers and studios their independence — while FreeWheel, the ad-serving spine of premium video, stays behind with Comcast.
lead.body: Comcast said on June 29 it will separate NBCUniversal and Sky into an independent, publicly traded company through a tax-free spinoff, leaving Comcast focused on broadband, cable and wireless. The new media company will hold Universal Pictures, the NBC and Telemundo networks, streaming service Peacock, Bravo, the theme parks and UK broadcaster Sky, with co-CEO Mike Cavanagh becoming its chief executive; the split is expected to close in about a year. Crucially for the ad market, Comcast retains its core technology business — including FreeWheel, the ad-serving infrastructure that monetizes premium video for hundreds of media companies — and has not said what commercial agreement, if any, will govern FreeWheel's relationship with a separated NBCUniversal. The move reshapes one of the largest owners of premium CTV and streaming inventory, and a standalone NBCU under pressure to monetize Peacock is likely to lean harder into advanced-TV ad products and outcomes deals. For programmatic buyers, the open question is whether the plumbing and the inventory it serves are about to answer to two different owners.

stories.headline: Samsung Opens Smart TV Home Screen to Programmatic Buyers
stories.dek: The Trade Desk and DV360 gain access via Magnite's SpringServe, with a global rollout beginning in Q3.
stories.body: Samsung Ads said its smart TV home-screen inventory is now buyable programmatically through DSPs including The Trade Desk and Google's DV360, powered by Magnite's SpringServe, with a global rollout across the US, EMEA and LATAM starting in Q3 2026. Samsung reaches more than 77 million active Smart TV households and calls it the largest programmatically accessible home-screen pool of its kind. The move pushes the highest-value real estate on the television — the first screen a viewer sees — into automated buying, intensifying the fight among Samsung, Roku, Amazon and LG for CTV's most premium surface.

stories.headline: Amazon Pushes Fire TV Home Screen as Prime Video Viewing Climbs
stories.dek: A redesigned interface and a World Cup hub frame Amazon's bid for home-screen ad dollars.
stories.body: Amazon began shipping a redesigned Fire TV interface built around content discovery and a 2026 FIFA World Cup hub across its Fire TV Sticks, the Fire TV Cube and Ember smart TVs globally, positioning home-screen placements as a captive-audience ad surface. The company said Prime Video ad-supported customers now watch 17% more hours each month than a year ago, and touted more than 90% incremental reach when home-screen units are paired with Prime Video commercials. With most Fire TV placements now buyable through Amazon's DSP, the refresh sharpens Amazon's head-to-head fight with Samsung and Roku for the TV operating system buyers most want programmatic access to.

stories.headline: Disney Ties Compass Clean Room to Affinity Card-Spend Data
stories.dek: Debit- and credit-card transaction signals feed planning and outcome measurement across Disney's streaming inventory.
stories.body: Disney unveiled a commerce-media capability with Affinity Solutions that layers historic purchase data from debit and credit card transactions onto Disney's audience graph, offering attribution and purchase insight across categories including retail and QSR through Disney's Compass clean room. Disney manages activation and distribution of the Affinity data across its properties, alongside existing Compass connections to LiveRamp, Snowflake and VideoAmp. The deal deepens the industry push to make premium CTV inventory measurable against real sales rather than proxy metrics, matching retail-data moves from Roku, Amazon and Walmart — and hands buyers another reason to grade streaming spend on outcomes.

stories.headline: Omnicom Measures Ad Frequency Across Rival Streamers in One Clean Room
stories.dek: A publisher-passed Creative ID lets a single instance track reach and frequency across Disney, NBCU and Paramount.
stories.body: Omnicom unveiled capabilities in its cross-platform clean room that measure reach, frequency and performance across multiple streaming publishers and linear broadcasters in a single instance, built on the Acxiom identity infrastructure it gained through the IPG acquisition and powered in part by The Trade Desk. It is live with Disney, NBCUniversal, Paramount and a range of VOD and FAST partners, and relies on a publisher-embedded Creative ID passed back into the clean room — a first for major CTV publishers. Frequency capping across walled-off streamers is one of CTV's most persistent buyer complaints, so a holdco-scale fix the biggest publishers actually feed data into is a real step toward cross-platform accountability.

stories.headline: Gracenote and PubMatic Bring Content-Level, Live-Sports Deals to CTV
stories.dek: Episode-level data matched at auction through the IAB Tech Lab's Agentic Real-Time Framework.
stories.body: Gracenote, Nielsen's content-intelligence business, and PubMatic announced a partnership matching bid opportunities against Gracenote episode-level data in real time, letting advertiser-selected inventory be tied to curated deal IDs and live-sports schedules. The integration runs on the IAB Tech Lab's Agentic Real-Time Framework inside PubMatic's AgenticOS, adding a fraction of a millisecond to each transaction. It targets a well-documented barrier — the 86% of media planners who cite thin show- or content-level data as a reason budgets stay in linear rather than CTV.

stories.headline: Yahoo DSP Adds Comscore, VideoAmp and iSpot Ahead of Upfronts
stories.dek: Video currencies jockeyed for position at Cannes as fall commitments loomed.
stories.body: Video ad currencies and outcomes measurement dominated Cannes Lions 2026, with providers racing to lock in business as upfront negotiations heated up. Yahoo's DSP added CTV measurement integrations with Comscore, VideoAmp and iSpot, to be completed by fall when upfront spend takes effect, while Nielsen touted currency upgrades combining panels with larger datasets. The scramble underscores that CTV still lacks a single standardized currency — and every DSP-level integration chips away at incumbent dominance while giving buyers more ways to grade streaming spend.

stories.headline: Publicis and The Trade Desk Settle Months-Long Fee Dispute
stories.dek: The holdco reinstates TTD to its recommended DSP list; shares jumped roughly 6% on the news.
stories.body: Publicis and The Trade Desk resolved a dispute that began in March, when Publicis pulled TTD from its recommended DSP list over how it applied ad-tech fees and told clients to pause spend. Neither side detailed the terms of the truce. With the settlement, and against the backdrop of the Fox–Roku deal, TTD shares rose about 6% on June 26. Because Publicis directs enormous advertiser budgets, its recommendation status is central to TTD's CTV revenue pipeline — and the episode shows how aggressively holdcos will now police ad-tech fee transparency.

stories.headline: PubMatic Launches Programmatic CTV Marketplace for Creators
stories.dek: MeatEater is the first partner in an auction that opens indie creator inventory to agentic demand.
stories.body: PubMatic unveiled its Creator Marketplace, billed as the first programmatic CTV auction connecting independent creator media companies' premium inventory with programmatic and emerging agentic demand. MeatEater is the launch partner, with FreeWheel as ad server and Holmes Media handling supply-side scaling. The move extends programmatic pipes to creator-led CTV audiences long confined to direct sponsorships and walled gardens, opening a new supply lane just as agentic buying scales.

stories.headline: Texas ACR Suits Against Smart-TV Makers Advance, Testing CTV Data Model
stories.dek: Paxton's cases against Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense and TCL target viewing-data collection at its source.
stories.body: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton's lawsuits against Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense and TCL — alleging unlawful collection and monetization of viewing data via automated content recognition without adequate consent — continue to advance, with temporary restraining orders already obtained against Hisense and Samsung. The AG seeks injunctive relief, restitution and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, and the ACR focus is expected to remain a state-enforcement priority through 2026. Because ACR-derived viewing data underpins much of CTV's targeting and measurement value, the litigation puts the smart-TV ad model itself on trial.

stories.headline: EU AI Act Content-Labelling Code Sets July 22 Signing Deadline
stories.dek: A voluntary transparency code precedes deepfake and AI-content labelling duties that bind on August 2.
stories.body: The European AI Office published the final Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content, with a July 22 deadline to be listed among initial signatories and Article 50 transparency obligations becoming applicable August 2. The code calls for clear labelling of deepfakes and AI-generated content on matters of public interest, recommending digitally signed metadata and imperceptible watermarking. As generative-AI creative floods CTV and political streaming ads, the labelling regime creates near-term compliance duties for any advertiser or platform serving AI-produced spots into the EU.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Strikes Party Spending Caps as Midterm Money Surges
stories.dek: A 6-3 ruling in NRSC v. FEC lets party committees spend unlimited sums in coordination with candidates — including on ads.
stories.body: On June 30 the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC that federal limits on coordinated party expenditures violate the First Amendment, striking caps that had ranged from about $65,000 for House races to as much as $4 million for Senate candidates. Effective immediately, national and state party committees may spend unlimited amounts in full coordination with a federal candidate on any campaign expense, advertising explicitly included. AdImpact already projects the 2026 cycle at $11.6 billion with connected TV the only major channel growing, at $2.7 billion — and removing a spending ceiling right before the election clears the way for more of that money to pour into streaming and broadcast inventory.

stories.headline: Sky Agrees Terms to Buy ITV's Broadcast and Streaming Arm for £1.6bn
stories.dek: Comcast-owned Sky would absorb ITVX; ITV Studios spins out as a standalone producer.
stories.body: Sky, owned by Comcast, has agreed terms to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment division — including the ITVX streaming service — in a deal reported at roughly £1.6 billion, with ITV Studios carved out as a standalone production business and a formal announcement expected within weeks. The transaction would still need clearance from the CMA, Ofcom and the UK culture secretary. A combined Sky-plus-ITV ad-sales operation could control well over half the UK TV ad market, concentrating British premium-video and addressable CTV supply under one owner just as the separate Sky–Channel 4–ITV joint marketplace comes online.

stories.headline: TAM: JioHotstar Leads IPL 2026 CTV Ads at 35%, Google Second
stories.dek: Connected TV drew a distinct, tech- and e-commerce-heavy advertiser base separate from linear.
stories.body: TAM Sports' IPL 2026 report found Star India/JioHotstar topped connected-TV ad volumes at 35% over the tournament's opening 22 matches, with Google second at 20% and Havells, Renault and Reliance Consumer Products rounding out the top five. E-commerce, media and social categories dominated CTV at 35% of volumes, while linear TV stayed FMCG-led, and the report noted CTV drew more advertisers running exclusively on the medium than linear did. The split confirms Indian CTV is building its own demand pool rather than mirroring broadcast — a signal for how the market's ad currency and pricing will develop.

stories.headline: Brazil and Mexico Outpace US on CTV Adoption, Amagi Report Finds
stories.dek: LATAM's anchor markets top the mature US on connected-TV reach as FAST scales into a World Cup year.
stories.body: Amagi's latest FAST report finds Brazil and Mexico posting higher CTV adoption than the US, with survey work across Brazil, Argentina and Mexico showing 91% of TV viewers streaming weekly and 79% receptive to ads in exchange for free or lower-cost content. Growth is driven by smart-TV uptake, global and local streamers, and expanding FAST services, alongside a steep rise in regional ad impressions. The findings reinforce LATAM as a top-tier CTV growth region and a receptive ad environment, drawing more global sellers and DSPs into the market.

stories.headline: Bell Media Extends Live CTV Sports Inventory West via TELUS Deal
stories.dek: Addressable live inventory on TSN and CTV now reaches TELUS TV+ across Western Canada.
stories.body: Bell Media struck a strategic agreement with TELUS to expand its live connected-TV advertising into Western Canada across TSN, CTV and leading English-language specialty channels on the TELUS TV+ platform, giving advertisers national scale. TSN's live CoTV inventory alone delivers more than 50 million monthly impressions with addressable targeting via 70 pre-built segments and Bell Audience Manager, part of a reported 350% expansion of Bell's CTV inventory. Digitizing live linear sports for addressable buying is Canada's most concrete move yet toward programmatic premium-sports CTV supply.

stories.headline: Nexxen and VIDAA Open Hisense Smart-TV Inventory for World Cup
stories.dek: Programmatic access to the Hisense/Toshiba OS footprint, as Channel 4 buys home-screen space on the same platform.
stories.body: Nexxen and V — formerly VIDAA, the Hisense-owned smart-TV operating system — announced a partnership letting advertisers programmatically plan and activate live-sports campaigns across V's global Hisense and Toshiba footprint for summer 2026 via Nexxen's DSP and SSP. In parallel, Channel 4 moved into VIDAA home-screen advertising, selling premium placements across VIDAA-powered Hisense, Toshiba and Loewe sets. The moves open a major Chinese-OEM smart-TV OS to Western programmatic demand, expanding global CTV supply beyond Samsung and Roku ahead of the World Cup.

stories.headline: Paparo Maps the Walmart–Vibe Winners and Losers
stories.body: Ari Paparo argues Walmart's $1.4B Vibe.co buy validates performance/SMB CTV as net-new budget with 'little sign of a ceiling,' names MNTN and Tatari as the next acquisition targets, and flags The Trade Desk as a loser now that Walmart owns its own CTV buying platform. It reframes the deal from a retail-media story into a signal that self-serve performance TV is the sector's hottest M&A category.

stories.headline: OpenAI at Cannes: 'We Are Clearly in the Advertising Business Now'
stories.body: At its first-ever Cannes Lions, OpenAI declared it is now in the advertising business — a marker of how fast generative-AI platforms are moving toward ad-supported models. For CTV, a serious OpenAI ad push raises the prospect of AI-native formats and planning tools competing for the video budgets agencies are already redirecting toward advanced TV.

stories.headline: The Set That Watches Back
stories.dek: We thought we bought a window. We installed an eye.
stories.body:
For seventy years the television was the thing we looked at. Reverse the figure and the ground, and the news of this season snaps into focus: the television is now the thing that looks at us. Automated content recognition does not display content — it reads the room. The home screen is not a menu; it is a face, turned toward the viewer, learning. What the smart set senses is no longer what it shows.

This is not surveillance in the old sense of a camera in the corner. The screen has no motive; it is simply doing what every electric medium does — extending a sense until the sense reverses on its owner. The eye we built to see the program has become the program's eye. Texas calls this spying and reaches for the law. But the law arrives to a scene already transformed: the set is a nervous system, and the household has been wired into it as an organ, not an audience.

Notice what the shoppable remote completes. The old distance between watching and wanting — the gap the whole grammar of the commercial depended on — collapses to a button. To see is to buy; to sit is to be read. The living room, once the most private theatre in the culture, is now its most attentive instrument. We did not lose our privacy to the television. We handed it our senses, and asked to be recognized.

— Marshall McLuhan

stories.headline: The Reckoning Comes to the Glamour Medium
stories.dek: Television is at last being asked the only question that matters: did it sell?
stories.body:
I began my life in advertising with direct mail — the despised, the unglamorous, the guttersnipe of our trade. I loved it for one reason. It kept score. Every coupon returned or unreturned told me, without mercy or flattery, whether my copy had done its work. The rest of advertising floated above such indignities, and television floated highest of all: the beautiful thirty seconds, admired at Cannes, measured by nobody.

That era is closing, and good riddance. When a streamer now welds card-spend data to its inventory, and an agency counts reach and frequency across rival platforms in one accounting, television is being dragged down to where direct mail always lived — the place where you must prove you sold something. The politicians have already noticed; connected TV is the one channel of a $11.6 billion election cycle that is still growing, because it can be held to account for a vote the way I was held to account for an order.

Do not mourn the loss of mystique. The advertiser who tells you performance measurement kills creativity is confessing that his creativity never sold anything. Great selling and hard proof have never been enemies; only lazy men pretend they are. I once sold Rolls-Royce on a single measured fact about a clock, not on a mood. The same discipline is now arriving in the living room, and the copywriter who cannot survive it was never selling in the first place. Television has spent seventy years as our most expensive entertainment. Make it, at last, our most accountable salesman.

— David Ogilvy

what_to_watch: The next fault line is structural: Comcast's decision to keep FreeWheel while spinning off NBCUniversal and Sky forces the question of whether ad-serving infrastructure and premium inventory can serve two masters — watch for the commercial terms that govern their split. In the UK, the CMA, Ofcom and the culture secretary now hold the fate of Sky's £1.6bn move on ITV, a deal that would put more than half the British TV ad market under one roof. And in Washington, the Supreme Court's removal of coordinated party-spending caps lands with the 2026 cycle already at a record pace — expect the freed dollars to test connected TV's capacity as the only political channel still growing.
